notes: THE FIELD IS NO LONGER SATURATED, AND THE STRIDE ALONE IS WHY. The premise this file was built on -- TEACHER-PIPELINE.md's '99.8% of pixels change by more than 1% of maximum, in every frame, in every session' -- was measured on torn frames. At the correct stride the raw variant's saturation on condition A is 0.5999 and on the empty capture 0.0154, against 0.9973 and 0.4173 before. The empty room is no longer a saturated field at all.

THE COMPOSITION NO LONGER BUYS ANYTHING, because there is nothing left to remove. The A-vs-C signal-to-noise ratio is 1.410 raw and 1.389 for the most aggressive composition -- the filters move the SNR by less than 0.03, where before the raw variant was 1.99 and the composition 1.83. The filter sweep has become a measurement of filter cost, not filter benefit.

LOCALISATION IMPROVED. The share of the excess that falls in the most active 5% of pixels goes from 42.8% on the raw variant, against 24.9% before. Random would be 5%. The speech signal is more localised, not less, once the torn frames are out of the way.

frame_layout.note: the captures on disk carry 19,200 bytes per frame (a 160x96 luma plane followed by 80x24 INTERLEAVED U,V samples), not the W*H*3//2 = 23,040 of a standard NV12 frame. The layout is DETECTED per file by src/nv12.py; see src/nv12.py

verdict: THE FILTERS ARE NOT NEEDED, AND THE PREMISE IS WITHDRAWN. At the correct stride the motion field is not saturated: the raw variant's saturation is 0.5999 on condition A and 0.0154 on the empty capture, against 0.9973 and 0.4173 before the stride fix. The composition of row-band removal with a temporal median does not improve the speech signal-to-noise ratio -- 1.410 raw against 1.389 for the most aggressive variant -- because there is no longer a nuisance for either of them to remove. The honest recommendation is to use the raw representation, keep the zero latency, and re-run the teacher on it.

supersedes.why: Re-measured on 2026-10-20. The previous run read every capture at W*H*3//2 = 23,040 bytes per frame; the captures on disk carry 19,200 bytes per frame, so all but every sixth frame was torn (rows 0..71 from frame k, rows 72..95 from frame k+1). The previous numbers are recorded here rather than silently overwritten.
supersedes.previous_limits_note: the previous run read the corpus metadata from /mnt/c/proart_capture/corpus, whose per-condition JSON still carries the wrong-stride 'n_frames: 600, seconds: 20.0'. This run reads corpus_v2, which was re-seeded at the correct stride and records n_frames 900, seconds 30.0. The source captures are the same files, so the only numerical change is the stride fix itself.

limits: two labelled sessions per class; the composition can make a teacher MORE LIKELY to pass its gate but cannot make one pass
the empty capture is later and darker than the occupied ones
the flip rates here are computed on the motion maps, not on the Braille field, so they are not directly comparable to the 50.00% / 0.01% figures in the other documents
